summary: Part II of the p-adic local Langlands roadmap for GL₂(ℚ_p): discharge of the global hypotheses of the base §6.9 and the realisation for every supercuspidal type in the p-central sector; P-finite Kirillov, embedded-dual, covariance and irreducibility refinements and Colmez's weight change; the geometric fundamental diagram and the Galois and Banach multiplicities of p-adic étale cohomology of the Drinfeld tower; the integral block decomposition and the factorisation over full Weil–Deligne type rings for p > 3; weighted, Iwasawa, primitive, derived and boundary consequences.

nodes.title: Discrete-series types and the two level conventions
nodes.statement: Define ΦN, ΦNᵖ and ΦNᵖ_n as in Conventions, using GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3 for the rank-two discrete-series parameters and `DivisionAlgebraTypes.jacquetLanglands` (base roadmap §6.9) for JL. A supercuspidal geometric M has rank two, N = 0 and slope 1/2. A special M is Sp⊗δ with N ≠ 0, and then JL(M) = δ∘Nrd. The DLB cover Σ_r is the CDN level 2r. The p-central quotient and its Weil descent are those of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison §§12.14 and 12.19 (CDN23 lines 2339–2349; DLB17 lines 104–106).

api.statement: M has level at most n exactly when JL(M) factors through Ǧ/(1+ϖ_D^nO_D). Level at most n implies level at most m for every m ≥ n, compatibly with pullback along the tower.
M lies in ΦNᵖ exactly when the p-central quotient has a nonzero JL(M)-multiplicity space for some n. For special M = Sp⊗δ this means δ(p)² = 1, since p ∈ Z(Ǧ) has reduced norm p².
The DLB cover Σ_r is the CDN level 2r, with the same central sector.

tests.statement: At r = 1, 1+pO_D = 1+ϖ_D²O_D, which is strictly smaller than 1+ϖ_DO_D. Identifying DLB level r with CDN level r would put the first ϖ_D-cover in place of Σ_1.
For special M = Sp⊗δ, JL(M) = δ∘Nrd is one-dimensional and N ≠ 0. A construction that requires a rank-two absolutely irreducible Galois family rejects it.

Take a supercuspidal π₀ with trivial central character and the unramified character χ with χ(p) = 1+p, and put M = M(π₀⊗χ∘det). Then JL(M) = JL(π₀)⊗χ∘Nrd, so p acts on JL(M) by χ(p²) = (1+p)² ≠ 1. Hence M has the level of π₀ but does not lie in ΦNᵖ, and every Ǧ-map from JL(M) into the p-central quotient vanishes.

nodes.title: Type decomposition and multiplicity spaces
nodes.statement: The base roadmap §6.9 defines X^ρ for one ρ, with its evaluation isomorphism ρ⊗X^ρ ≅ e_ρX. Here the decomposition is over all types. Let Z be a smooth L[Ǧ]-module on which p acts trivially and whose action factors through Ǧ/(p^ℤ(1+ϖ_D^nO_D)), and let L split all irreducible representations of this finite group. Prove that evaluation gives a Ǧ-equivariant isomorphism ⊕_{M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n} Z[M]⊗_L JL(M) → Z, where Ǧ acts trivially on Z[M]. For a topological G×Ǧ-representation the isomorphism is topological, each Z[M] carrying the subspace topology of Hom_L(JL(M), Z). Prove that a continuous equivariant map induces maps on every Z[M], compatibly with composition, and that the decomposition commutes with finite extension of L. Source: CDN23 lines 2346–2349; DLB17, Théorème 1.2 and its footnote on σ^ρ (DLB17 line 154).

api.statement: Evaluation ⊕_M Z[M]⊗JL(M) → Z is a topological isomorphism. Only finitely many M have Z[M] ≠ 0.
A continuous G×Ǧ-map Z → Z′ induces G-maps Z[M] → Z′[M] that respect identity and composition.
On strong duals Ǧ acts by (dℓ)(v) = ℓ(d⁻¹v). A central element acting on Z[M] by a scalar acts on the dual by its inverse.
Finite extension L′/L commutes with Z[M] and with the decomposition.

tests.statement: For Z = W⊗JL(M) with trivial Ǧ-action on W, Z[M] = W⊗End(JL(M)) = W, not W⊗JL(M). When dim JL(M) = 2 the second space has twice the dimension.

For absolutely irreducible JL(M) ≇ JL(M′), Hom_Ǧ(JL(M), JL(M′)) = 0 over a splitting field. Taking the full isotypic projector in place of the multiplicity space would keep a nonscalar End(JL(M)) acting.
If z ∈ Z(G) acts on E by χ(z), it acts on E′_b by χ(z)⁻¹. Omitting the inverse in the dual action fails this computation.

nodes.title: The period-line parameter
nodes.statement: For a supercuspidal M of slope 1/2 over L⊗ℚ_p^nr, put M_dR = (ℚ̄_p⊗_{ℚ_p^nr}M)^{G_ℚ_p}, a two-dimensional L-space. Put X⁺_st(M) = (B⁺_cris⊗_{ℚ_p^nr}M)^{φ=p}. For an L-line ℒ ⊂ M_dR, define V_{M,ℒ} as the kernel of the map X⁺_st(M) → C⊗(M_dR/ℒ) induced by θ. Prove the following (CDN20, §2.1.4, lines 879–885; Remarque 2.6 and Lemme 2.7, lines 889–913):

api.statement: V_{M,ℒ} is the θ-preimage of C⊗ℒ in X⁺_st(M); its dimension is two and it is absolutely irreducible.
Hom_{G_ℚ_p}(V_{M,ℒ}, X⁺_st(M)) is one-dimensional over L.
A finite extension L′/L transports M, ℒ and V_{M,ℒ} compatibly.
Distinct lines give non-isomorphic representations.

tests.statement: For fixed M and ℒ ≠ ℒ′, V_{M,ℒ} ≇ V_{M,ℒ′}, although both have D_pst ≅ M[−1]. The unfiltered module does not determine V.
C⊗V_{M,ℒ} ≅ (L⊗C) ⊕ (L⊗C)(1) (CDN20, Remarque 2.8, line 914), so the weights are {0,1}. A construction that returned a character would give a one-dimensional C-semilinear representation.
The shift M[−1] is witnessed on ℚ_p(1): D_pst(ℚ_p(1)) has φ = p⁻¹, and its shift [1] has φ = 1. Dropping the shift would identify M with D_pst(V) and change every φ-eigenvalue by a factor p.

nodes.title: The normalisation dictionary among the three sources
nodes.statement: The base roadmap §6.9(i) parametrises V(π) by ℙ(M_dR(π)) through Π ↦ Fil⁰D_dR(V(Π)), where M(π) comes from the classical correspondence normalised à la Tate. DLB17 writes the de Rham comparison with M*_dR(π) and the orthogonal ℒ^⊥. CDN20 writes it with the geometric module M = D_pst(V)[1], with M_dR and ℒ. Prove the dictionary between them. Let π be supercuspidal with central character ζ and ζ(p) = 1, and let M be the CDN module with LL(M) = π. Then:

tests.statement: For a basis e₁, e₂ of M_dR and ℒ = Le₁, the map v ↦ (w ↦ v∧w) sends e₁ to the functional that kills e₁ and sends e₂ to e₁∧e₂. So ℒ goes to Le₂*⊗∧²M_dR = ℒ^⊥⊗∧²M_dR. Using ℒ itself in M*_dR would give the wrong preimage.
Twisting by an unramified character μ with μ(p) = −1 changes ζ by μ² = 1 at p. It leaves the ℒ-dictionary unchanged and multiplies the φ-eigenvalues on M by −1.
For V = V_{M,ℒ}, Fil⁰D_dR(V) is one-dimensional and Fil¹D_dR(V) = 0, since the jumps are −1 and 0. Taking Fil¹ instead of Fil⁰ as the parameter would give the zero space.

nodes.title: The unfiltered equation of a supercuspidal family
nodes.statement: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology §5.6a constructs N_rig(V) for each de Rham V, and the base roadmap §4.2a uses it for one M. Here prove the family statements. For V, V′ in the family of π there is an isomorphism N_rig(V) ≅ N_rig(V′), unique up to L^×, compatible with φ, Γ and ∂ = t⁻¹∇. Write N_rig(π) for the common object. For n large, N⁺_dif,n = L_n[[t]]⊗_L M_dR and D⁺_dif,n(V_{M,ℒ}) = tN⁺_dif,n + L_n[[t]]⊗ℒ. Hence tN_rig(π) ⊂ D_rig(V_{M,ℒ}) ⊂ N_rig(π), with the same radius qualification on each term. Prove these from the characterisation of N_rig by its localisations (DLB17, Exemple 6.5 and Exemple 6.6 with Définition 6.7, lines 1335–1345) and from Fil⁰(L_n((t))⊗D_dR(V)) = Σ_i t^{−i}L_n[[t]]⊗Fil^iD_dR(V). These are the inclusions used in PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology §5.7.

tests.statement: The quotient N⁺_dif,n/D⁺_dif,n is L_n⊗(M_dR/ℒ), killed by t. Two distinct lines give the same N⁺_dif,n but distinct D⁺_dif,n.

For V = V_{M,ℒ}, the filtration has Fil⁻¹ = M_dR, Fil⁰ = ℒ and Fil¹ = 0, so Σ_i t^{−i}Fil^i = tN⁺ + L_n[[t]]ℒ. With jumps 0 and 1 instead, the same formula would give N⁺ + t⁻¹L_n[[t]]ℒ ⊃ N⁺, which is not contained in N⁺.
For weights {0,k} with k ≥ 2, the same computation gives D⁺ ⊃ t^kN⁺, not tN⁺. The sandwich tN ⊂ D ⊂ N is a weight-{0,1} statement.

nodes.title: Polynomial injectivity and invertibility of the connection
nodes.statement: Let V be absolutely irreducible, two-dimensional and nontrianguline. Prove that P(∇) is injective on D_rig(V) for every nonzero P ∈ L[X] (DLB17, Lemme 6.3, line 1250). The proof has two steps. First prove that the kernel X of P(∇) on D_rig(V) is finite-dimensional over L, by factoring P over a finite extension and bounding ker(∇−a) on each radius stage. Then use φ-stability of X: if X ≠ 0, φ has an eigenvector on D_rig(V) after a finite extension of L, which gives a rank-one (φ,Γ)-submodule and contradicts nontriangulinity. If moreover V is de Rham, ∂ = t⁻¹∇ is bijective on N_rig(V). This is DLB17 Proposition 6.4 (line 1259) and is supplied by PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology §RD.2.43, application step. No continuity statement for ∂⁻¹ is asserted. The theorem does not apply to trianguline V.

tests.statement: For the rank-one trivial equation R with ∇ = t(1+T)d/dT, P(X) = X kills 1, so the nontrianguline hypothesis cannot be dropped.
For V trianguline, D_rig(V) contains a rank-one submodule R(δ) with basis e, and ∇e = κ(δ)e, where κ(δ) is the weight of δ. So P(X) = X−κ(δ) kills e ≠ 0, and the injectivity fails.
For V of weights {0,1}, take h = 1 with tN_rig ⊂ D_rig. Then (∇−1)(tx) = t²∂x, so injectivity of ∂ on N_rig follows from injectivity of ∇−1 on D_rig.

nodes.title: P-finite vectors and infinite slope
nodes.statement: For a locally analytic representation Π of G on an L-space, define Π^{P-fin} to be the vectors v such that some power (u(p^n)−1)^k kills v and the orbit of v under diag(ℤ_p^×,1) spans a finite-dimensional space. Call v of infinite slope when there are n, k ≥ 1 and m ∈ ℤ with (Σ_{i=0}^{p^n−1} u(i))^k diag(p^m,1)v = 0. Put Π_c^{P-fin} for the intersection (DLB17, Définition 7.4 and Remarque 7.5, lines 1473–1500). The definition applies to every locally analytic G-representation and every prime. It specialises to the base roadmap §4.9's compactly supported P-finite space on Banach objects with supersingular constituents, where p ≥ 5.

api.statement: Π^{P-fin} and Π_c^{P-fin} are P-stable L-subspaces containing 0.
A continuous G-map carries P-finite vectors to P-finite vectors and infinite-slope vectors to infinite-slope vectors.
For v P-finite and N divisible enough, a power of 1−u(p^N) carries v into Π_c^{P-fin} (DLB17, Remarque 7.5).

tests.statement: The zero vector satisfies both conditions.
A nonzero vector v of the trivial representation is P-finite but not of infinite slope: the trace Σ_{i<p^n} u(i) acts by p^n, so its k-th power sends v to p^{nk}v ≠ 0.

For the Kirillov models of §1.4, a function supported on a single valuation shell is of infinite slope. A function with nonzero values on infinitely many shells accumulating at 0 is not in Π_c^{P-fin}.

nodes.title: Locally polynomial Kirillov function spaces
nodes.statement: For a Γ-module X killed by a power of t and on which t acts nilpotently, as for D⁻_dif(V) = lim_n D⁺_dif,n[1/t]/D⁺_dif,n, define LP(ℚ_p^×, X)^Γ. Its elements are the functions φ: ℚ_p^× → X with φ(ax) = σ_a(φ(x)) for a ∈ ℤ_p^× whose support has compact closure in ℚ_p; zero may be a limit point of the support. Define LP_c(ℚ_p^×, X)^Γ by requiring compact support in ℚ_p^×. Let (a b; 0 1) act by φ ↦ (x ↦ ε(bx) e^{tbx} φ(ax)), where ε is the additive character of ℚ_p fixed by the chosen p-power roots of unity (DLB17 lines 1531–1534). The exponential is a finite sum on each value because t is nilpotent on X.

api.statement: A Γ-equivariant function is determined by its values φ(p^j), j ∈ ℤ, and evaluation identifies LP_c(ℚ_p^×, X)^Γ with ⊕_{j∈ℤ} X.
LP_c ⊂ LP is a P-stable inclusion. It is not surjective as soon as X ≠ 0.
A Γ-equivariant map X → X′ commuting with t induces a P-equivariant map on LP and LP_c.
The formula defines a left action of P.

tests.statement: A Γ-equivariant function supported on p^jℤ_p^× has exactly one nonzero valuation coordinate.
The function equal to a fixed nonzero x on p^jℤ_p^× for every j ≥ 0 has support with closure ℤ_p, compact in ℚ_p but not in ℚ_p^×. So it lies in LP and not in LP_c.
Differentiating the action of u(b) at b = 0 multiplies φ(x) by tx. With the opposite order of the matrix factors the derivative of the a-action would be wrong by the sign of the Lie bracket.

nodes.title: The P-finite Kirillov model and the infinitesimal action
nodes.statement: For V in the family of π, construct the P-equivariant injection v ↦ φ_v: Π(V)^{P-fin} → LP(ℚ_p^×, D⁻_dif(V))^Γ. Prove that it restricts to an isomorphism Π(V)_c^{P-fin} ≅ LP_c(ℚ_p^×, D⁻_dif(V))^Γ (DLB17, Proposition 7.6, line 1535). This extends the base roadmap §4.1k, which treats P-algebraic vectors only. For generalized Hodge–Tate weights a, b, prove that U(gl₂) acts on D_rig(V) by a⁺ = ∇, a⁻ = a+b−1−∇, u⁺ = t and u⁻ = −t⁻¹(∇−a)(∇−b), with Casimir ((a−b)²−1)/2 (DLB17, Théorème 7.3, line 1460). In weights {0,1}, u⁻ = −t∂². The route takes the analytic-vector exact sequence of the base §3.11, Colmez's P-finite expansion, and the Sen operator for the Lie action.

tests.statement: At (a,b) = (0,1), the Casimir is ((0−1)²−1)/2 = 0. Also (∇−0)(∇−1) = t²∂², so u⁻ = −t⁻¹t²∂² = −t∂², not −∂²t.

For a P-finite vector in the image of the base roadmap's P-algebraic model, φ_v agrees with `Kirillov.compactPAlgebraic`. A second normalisation of the exponential would disagree already on u(b) at b = 1.
The zero vector maps to the zero function. By injectivity, a vector with zero Kirillov function is zero.

nodes.title: The differential residue pairing
nodes.statement: The pairing V̌×V → L(1) gives ⟨ , ⟩: D⁺_dif(V̌)[1/t] × D⁺_dif(V)[1/t] → L_∞((t))dt, where dt is the canonical basis of ℚ_p(1). Define {ž, z}_dif = lim_n p^{−n} res₀ Tr_{L_n((t))/L((t))} ⟨σ_{−1}(ž), z⟩, with res₀(Σ a_n t^n dt) = a_{−1} (DLB17 lines 1550–1564). Prove the following:

api.statement: The pairing is the normalised trace of the residue of the σ_{−1}-adjusted product, and is independent of n.
D⁺_dif is its own annihilator under the determinant identification when det V = χ.
(N⁺_dif(V̌))^⊥ = tN⁺_dif(V) for every de Rham V.

tests.statement: For V = L, V̌ = L(1) and N⁺(V̌) = L_∞[[t]]t⁻¹dt. The residue of f·g·t⁻¹dt is the constant term of fg, so the orthogonal of N⁺(V̌) is tL_∞[[t]] = tN⁺(L).
For weights {0,2}, te ∈ tN⁺(V) pairs to residue zero with every element of N⁺(V̌), but te ∉ t²N⁺(V). So the printed t^k fails at k = 2.
Only products of total t-exponent −1 contribute. A pairing without the normalisation p^{−n} would change by the factor p when n increases by one.

nodes.title: Kirillov duality and the smooth-vector criterion
nodes.statement: For V in the family of π, n ≥ m(V), v ∈ Π(V)_c^{P-fin} and ℓ ∈ (Π(V)^an)′_b, prove {ℓ, v}_{ℙ¹} = Σ_{j∈ℤ} {i_{j,n}(ℓ), φ_v(p^{−j})}_dif. Here i_{j,n} = φ^{−n}∘Res_ℤ_p∘diag(p^{n−j},1) (DLB17, Théorème 7.8, lines 1576–1586). Prove the following description of the smooth vectors (DLB17, Proposition 7.9 and Théorème 7.11, lines 1593–1615):

tests.statement: The nonzero trivial representation is P-smooth and killed by u⁺ and a⁺ but not of infinite slope (§1.3). Without the infinite-slope condition the criterion would wrongly include it.
For v supported on one shell p^jℤ_p^×, the sum has one nonzero term.
For the zero functional the sum vanishes term by term.

nodes.title: The common embedded analytic dual
nodes.statement: For V in the family of π, write B_V = (Π(V)^an/π)′_b with its canonical embedding into D_rig(V̌)⊠ℙ¹. Prove the following (DLB17, Proposition 8.2, Théorème 8.3 and Théorème 8.6, lines 1661–1690 and 1828):

tests.statement: The statement is an equality of subspaces of tN_rig(π)⊠ℙ¹ with their topologies. An abstract isomorphism B_V ≅ B_{V′}, which is the base §4.11, does not imply it.
An element of E_π with zero restriction to ℤ_p and zero restriction of its Weyl transform is zero. Vanishing of the ℤ_p-restriction alone does not imply this.
Lines Le₁ ≠ Le₂ give different Π(V)^an but the same E_π.

nodes.title: Homographic covariance of the coordinate operator
nodes.statement: Let ∂ be the operator on E_π of the base roadmap's `DrinfeldComparison.halfPlaneModule`, characterised by a⁺−1 = u⁺∂. Prove the following on E_π (DLB17, Proposition 9.6, Théorème 9.7 and Lemme 9.8, lines 1946–1980):

tests.statement: For w = (0 1; 1 0): det w = −1 and (0−∂)² = ∂², so w∂w = (−1)(−∂)⁻¹ = ∂⁻¹ and wu⁺w = −∂²u⁺. On O(Ω), with (wf)(z) = f(1/z) and u⁺f = −f′, the composite w u⁺ w sends f to z²f′, and −∂²u⁺f = −z²(−f′) agrees.
For u(b) = (1 b; 0 1), u(b)∂u(b)⁻¹ = ∂−b. On functions this is z ↦ z−b.
For aI₂ the conjugation factor is (a²)⁻¹a² = 1, consistent with the trivial central character.

nodes.title: Topological irreducibility of Π(π,0)
nodes.statement: Prove that Π(π,0) is topologically irreducible as a locally analytic G-representation. Equivalently, E_π has no nonzero proper closed G-stable subspace. Colmez proves that Π(M,−k) is irreducible for every absolutely irreducible M and k ≥ 1 (COLMEZ19POIDS, Théorème 0.3(ii), line 179). By COLMEZ19POIDS Remarque 0.2(ii) (lines 161–166) and Théorème 0.6(iii) at k = 1 (line 234), Π(V)^an is an extension of Π(M,−1)⊗det by LL_p(M) = π when V has weights {0,1}. Hence Π(π,0) ≅ Π(M,−1)⊗det, which is irreducible exactly when Π(M,−1) is. DLB17 Remarque 1.8 (line 410) records this result. Transport it to E_π by the anti-equivalence of the base roadmap §0.1.

tests.statement: The statement concerns the G-action alone. It is stronger than the irreducibility of O(Σ_r)^ρ as an O(Ω)[G]-semilinear module used for surjectivity in the base §6.9.
Π(V)^an itself is reducible, with the smooth subrepresentation π. Irreducibility is a property of the quotient, not of Π(V)^an.
For a trianguline V, Π(V)^an has a different Jordan–Hölder pattern (COLMEZ19POIDS, Remarque 0.2(ii), lines 158–160). The theorem is not asserted there.

nodes.title: Weight change
nodes.statement: Let M be a supercuspidal rank-two (φ,N,G_ℚ_p)-module, so that M is absolutely irreducible as a (φ,N,G_ℚ_p)-module, and let Δ = Δ(M) be the (φ,Γ)-module over the Robba ring of Hodge–Tate weights (0,0) attached to M. For M = M(π) with π as above, Δ is N_rig(π) of §1.1. Put ω = (x|x|)⁻¹det Δ, and write ⊗δ for the twist by δ∘det. For k ≥ 1 and a line ℒ ⊂ M_dR, let Δ_{k,ℒ} be the de Rham (φ,Γ)-module of weights (0,k) with t^kΔ ⊂ Δ_{k,ℒ} ⊂ Δ attached to ℒ (COLMEZ19POIDS lines 205–211). Every line is weakly admissible (§0.3), so Δ_{k,ℒ} = D_rig(V^{(k)}_{M,ℒ}) for an absolutely irreducible de Rham representation V^{(k)}_{M,ℒ} of weights {0,k}; up to the normalisations of §§0.3–0.4, the V^{(1)}_{M,ℒ} are the representations V_{M,ℒ′} of §0.3. This subsection does not assume a trivial central character. Prove the following (COLMEZ19POIDS, Théorème 0.6, lines 215–236, and Théorème 0.8, lines 262–271):

tests.statement: The central element aI₂ acts on Π(M,k) by a^kω(a), since (a−0·∂)^k = a^k. This agrees with (ii): Π(M,−k) has central character x^{−k}ω, so Π(M,−k)⊗x^k has x^{−k}ω·x^{2k} = x^kω, the central character of Δ⊠_{x^kω}ℙ¹. With (a−c∂)^{−k} in (iii), Π(M,k) would have central character x^{−k}ω and contradict (ii).

At k = 1, Π(M,1)^alg = M_dR⊗LL(M) is two copies of π. Its quotient by ℒ⊗π is Π(V^{(1)}_{M,ℒ})^an, whose smooth vectors (M_dR/ℒ)⊗π ≅ π form one copy, as for every member of V(π). The quotient Π(M,1)/Π(M,1)^alg ≅ Π(M,−1)⊗det is the analytic quotient of §2.3. For π with trivial central character, det Δ_{1,ℒ} = x·det Δ = x|x| gives ω = x⁻¹, and Π(M,−1)⊗det has central character x⁻²·x² = 1.
The Casimir on Δ⊠_{x^kω}ℙ¹ is (k²−1)/2: it is 0 at k = 1, matching §1.5 at weights (0,1), and −1/2 at k = 0. So the weight-(0,0) sheaf is not the sheaf of §4.2a, and the index k is not a relabelling.

nodes.title: Discharge of the global hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let π be supercuspidal with trivial central character, ρ = JL(π), and r such that ρ is trivial on 1+p^rO_D. Prove the two global inputs that the base roadmap §6.9 takes as explicit hypotheses:

tests.statement: The zero map is continuous and equivariant but does not discharge (a).
A map constructed for π⊗ξ∘det has Ǧ-sector JL(π)⊗ξ∘Nrd. When this is not isomorphic to ρ, the map does not land in O(Σ_r)^ρ.
Rescaling Φ by c ∈ L^× gives another valid map; the comparison of the base §6.9 is unique up to this scalar.

The twist in (a) can be removed: π(f)_p has central character ξ², which is the p-component of the finite-order central character of f, so ξ(p) is a root of unity. An unramified character with ξ(p) not a root of unity is the p-component of no finite-order global character.
For ρ trivial, the constant functions give H⁰_dR(Σ_r)^ρ ≠ 0 and the degeneration used in (b) fails. It is dim ρ ≥ 2, true for every supercuspidal π, that kills the ρ-parts of H⁰ and H².
The dimension in (b) is 2, not 1: the eigenspace of the proper curve has Hodge pieces of types (1,0) and (0,1). Counting holomorphic differentials alone gives 1.

nodes.title: The line-independent quotient Kirillov embedding
nodes.statement: Localisation and the identifications of §1.1 induce a P-equivariant embedding ι of the u⁺-kernel of Π(V)^an/π into LP(ℚ_p^×, t⁻¹N⁺_dif,∞/N⁺_dif,∞)^Γ. Prove that the embeddings for different V agree up to their comparison scalar (DLB17, Proposition 11.2, Théorème 11.3 and Lemmes 11.4–11.5, lines 2432–2524). The coefficient module t⁻¹N⁺/N⁺ is L_∞(−1)⊗M_dR(π), with Γ acting through χ⁻¹. The target is identified with locally constant L_∞⊗M_dR(π)-valued functions only after the twist of Π(π,2), in which the model takes values in the untwisted coefficient module (DLB17 lines 2449 and 2469–2472). The route compares the pairings on compactly supported functions by Lemme 11.4 and uses their nondegeneracy (Lemme 11.5).

tests.statement: γ ∈ Γ acts on the class of t⁻¹e in t⁻¹N⁺/N⁺ by χ(γ)⁻¹. Treating the target as locally constant functions before untwisting gives the wrong Γ-equivariance by this character.
The embedding is independent of V as an embedded P-module once the scalar is fixed, not merely as an abstract vector space.
On a vector supported on one shell the Kirillov function has one nonzero coordinate, in t⁻¹N⁺/N⁺.

nodes.title: The realisation for every supercuspidal type in the p-central sector
nodes.statement: Let M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n be supercuspidal, π = LL(M) with central character ζ, ζ(p) = 1, and ρ = JL(M). Do not assume that ζ is trivial. Prove the following for n with JL(M) trivial on 1+ϖ_D^nO_D:

tests.statement: At p = 7, let ω be the quadratic character of 𝔽₇^× extended by ω(7) = 1, and let π be supercuspidal with central character ω. The square of a character of μ₆ ⊂ ℤ₇^× has order dividing 3, while ω|μ₆ has order 2. So no twist π⊗χ∘det has trivial central character, and reduction to the base §6.9 by twisting is impossible. Since ω(7) = 1, M ∈ ΦNᵖ and the theorem applies.
For ζ = 1 and ℒ = Le₁, (ii) puts the preimage at Le₁⊗π′_b ⊂ M_dR⊗π′_b. The base §6.9(iii) puts it at Le₂*⊗π′_b ⊂ M*_dR⊗π′_b. The two agree under §0.4(c).
For M ∉ ΦNᵖ, for instance after the twist with χ(p) = 1+p of §0.1, both sides of (i) vanish on the p-central quotient. The statement must not be read on the full tower.

nodes.title: The fundamental diagram of the Drinfeld tower
nodes.statement: For supercuspidal M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n of slope 1/2, prove that there is a commutative diagram of G×G_ℚ_p-Fréchet spaces with exact rows (CDN20, Théorème 0.8, line 323, and Corollaire 2.1, line 762; CDN23 lines 2501–2514):

tests.statement: θ: X⁺_st(M) → C⊗M_dR is injective because M has slope 1/2 > 0, so (B⁺_cris⊗M)^{φ=1} = 0 (CDN20, Remarque 2.3, line 817). For a slope-zero module the φ = 1 invariants survive and the right vertical map fails to be injective.
Taking G_ℚ_p-invariants of the bottom row gives 0 → O[M]^{G_ℚ_p} → Ω¹[M]^{G_ℚ_p} → M_dR⊗LL(M)′_b → 0 (CDN20 lines 917–919).
For M ∉ ΦNᵖ all terms of both rows vanish on the p-central quotient.

nodes.title: Half-plane cohomology and the three Steinberg representations
nodes.statement: Define St^sm = C^sm(ℙ¹(ℚ_p), L)/L, St^cont = C⁰(ℙ¹(ℚ_p), L)/L and St^an = C^an(ℙ¹(ℚ_p), L)/L. Each carries the inverse-pullback G-action and the quotient topology, and their strong duals are the functionals of total mass zero (CDN20, §1.3, line 614). Prove that St^cont is the universal unitary completion of St^sm and of St^an (base roadmap §2.5). Prove the following on Ω (CDN20, Proposition 1.6 and Théorème 1.7, lines 659–680; Drinfeld for the étale statement):

api.statement: Each Steinberg form is the stated function space modulo constants, with the quotient topology, and its dual is the annihilator of the constants.
The maps St^sm → St^cont and St^an → St^cont have dense image and the universal property of unitary completion.
Twisting by δ commutes with the half-plane comparisons for δ_G, δ_Ǧ and δ simultaneously.

tests.statement: A constant function represents zero in all three quotients. δ_x − δ_y has total mass zero and is a nonzero element of each dual for x ≠ y, while δ_x alone does not vanish on the constants and is not in the dual.
The function z ↦ (z−a)/(z−b) has symbol mapped to δ_a − δ_b (CDN20, Proposition 1.5, line 650). Its residues at a and b are opposite, matching total mass zero.
The scalar aI₂ acts on St^cont⊗δ_G by δ(a²), and a ∈ ℚ_p^× ⊂ Ǧ acts by δ(Nrd a) = δ(a²). Both sides agree, and δ(p)² = 1 is exactly the ΦNᵖ condition.

nodes.title: Extension of a partial operator with prescribed spectrum
nodes.statement: Let E be a d-dimensional L-vector space, S ⊂ E a subspace and A: S → E an L-linear map such that the only subspace T ⊂ S with A(T) ⊂ T is T = 0. Prove that for any d pairwise distinct λ₁,…,λ_d ∈ L there is an endomorphism B of E extending A that has an eigenbasis e₁,…,e_d with Be_i = λ_ie_i (CDN20, Lemme 2.18, line 1171). No algebraic closure of L is assumed. The route inducts on d along a maximal A-chain s, As, A²s, … inside S, whose iterates up to the first exit from S are linearly independent. It completes the companion block with the coefficients of ∏(X−λ_i), which alternate in sign. The proof must establish that the complementary partial operator again has no nonzero invariant subspace before the induction applies; the source omits this step. The source prints all-positive companion coefficients (source correction E13).

tests.statement: d = 2, S = Le₁, Ae₁ = e₂. Then Be₂ = −λ₁λ₂e₁ + (λ₁+λ₂)e₂ gives trace λ₁+λ₂ and determinant λ₁λ₂. The all-positive column λ₁λ₂e₁ + (λ₁+λ₂)e₂ gives determinant −λ₁λ₂ and fails.
S = 0: every diagonal operator with the prescribed eigenbasis is an extension.
S = E with d ≥ 1 never satisfies the hypothesis, since T = E is A-stable. So the lemma never asks to extend a full endomorphism with no invariant subspace.

nodes.title: Period multiplicity spaces
nodes.statement: For finite F/ℚ_p, a finite-dimensional continuous L-representation V of G_F and a supercuspidal M of slope 1/2, define H_M(V) = Hom_{L[G_F]}(V, X⁺_st(M)) and H_C(V) = Hom_{L[G_F]}(V, L⊗_ℚ_p C) (CDN20, §2.1.2 and Remarque 2.3, lines 800–821). H_M(V) is finite-dimensional over L and H_C(V) is finite over L⊗F. θ induces an injection ι: H_M(V) → M_dR⊗_{L⊗F}H_C(V). The coefficients are L⊗_ℚ_p F, which is not identified with L when F ≠ ℚ_p.

api.statement: H_C(V) = (C⊗_ℚ_p V^∨)^{G_F} with its L⊗F-module structure.
ι is injective because M has positive slope.
A Galois map V → W induces H_M(W) → H_M(V) and H_C(W) → H_C(V), commuting with ι.

tests.statement: Both spaces vanish at V = 0.
For V = L trivial, H_C(L) = C^{G_F}⊗L = F⊗L.
For F = ℚ_p and V = V_{M,ℒ}, H_M(V) is one-dimensional and its θ-image is ℒ⊗H_C(V) ⊂ M_dR⊗H_C(V) (CDN20, Lemme 2.7, line 911).

nodes.title: The fundamental diagram after Galois multiplicities
nodes.statement: For supercuspidal M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n and finite-dimensional continuous V of G_ℚ_p, apply Hom_{G_ℚ_p}(V, −) to §4.1 and prove that the result is a commutative diagram with exact rows (CDN20, Proposition 2.4, line 822):

tests.statement: The left square is the identity on H_C(V)⊗O[M].
For V = 0 every term is 0.
dlog has closed image, which is needed to keep the middle term Fréchet. An abstract injection with nonclosed image would not give a strict sequence.

nodes.title: Classification of rank-two period multiplicities
nodes.statement: For finite F/ℚ_p, supercuspidal M and V a representation of G_F, prove the following (CDN20, Proposition 2.5, Remarque 2.6 and Lemme 2.7, lines 859–913):

tests.statement: A character V cannot embed in X⁺_st(M) for supercuspidal M, since M[−1]* has no one-dimensional WD-quotient.
For F = ℚ_p and V two-dimensional, the weight constraint κ₁, κ₂ ≥ 0 with κ₁+κ₂ = 1 forces weights {0,1}.
For F of degree two over ℚ_p, weights (0,0) at one embedding and (1,1) at the other satisfy the constraints but do not give a V_{M,ℒ}.

nodes.title: The line extension W_{M,ℒ}
nodes.statement: For supercuspidal M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n and a line ℒ ⊂ M_dR, let W′_{M,ℒ} be the preimage of ℒ⊗LL(M)′_b under Ω¹[M]^{G_ℚ_p} → M_dR⊗LL(M)′_b (§4.1). Let ℒ^{−1} = M*_dR/ℒ^⊥, so that ℒ^{−1}⊗ℒ = L canonically, and put W_{M,ℒ} = ℒ^{−1}⊗_L W′_{M,ℒ}. Its quotient is LL(M)′_b through evaluation (CDN20, §2.1.5, lines 917–951). Prove that W_{M,ℒ} ≅ (Π^an_{M,ℒ})′_b. This is CDN20 Proposition 2.9 (line 952), which the source deduces from DLB17 for trivial central character. Here it follows from §3.3(ii) for every M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n. Also prove Hom_{G_ℚ_p}(V_{M,ℒ}, H¹_proét[M]) ≅ W_{M,ℒ} (CDN20, Proposition 2.10, line 962).

api.statement: W′_{M,ℒ} is the full inverse image of ℒ⊗LL(M)′_b in Ω¹[M]^{G_ℚ_p}.
W_{M,ℒ} = ℒ^{−1}⊗W′_{M,ℒ}, whose quotient is LL(M)′_b through ℒ^{−1}⊗ℒ = L.
W_{M,ℒ} ≅ (Π^an_{M,ℒ})′_b, compatibly with the scalar of §3.3.
Hom_{G_ℚ_p}(V_{M,ℒ}, H¹_proét[M]) ≅ W_{M,ℒ}, respecting the G-action and the topology.

tests.statement: Replacing a generator e of ℒ by ae, a ∈ L^×, replaces the dual generator by a⁻¹e*. The normalised quotient map is unchanged.
For ℒ ≠ ℒ′, W′_{M,ℒ} ∩ W′_{M,ℒ′} = dO[M].
W′_{M,ℒ} ≠ Ω¹[M]^{G_ℚ_p}, since M_dR/ℒ ≠ 0 and LL(M) ≠ 0.

nodes.title: G-bounded vectors
nodes.statement: For a continuous L-linear action of G on a Hausdorff locally convex L-space E, call v ∈ E G-bounded when the orbit {gv : g ∈ G} is von Neumann bounded (Mathlib `Bornology.IsVonNBounded`). Write E^b for the G-bounded vectors (CDN23 lines 2378–2380; CDN20, §2.2.1, line 1009). If E is normed, this means the orbit has bounded norm (`NormedSpace.image_isVonNBounded_iff`). If the topology is given by seminorms (p_i), it means that for each i the values p_i(gv) are bounded, with a bound depending on i (`WithSeminorms.image_isVonNBounded_iff_seminorm_bounded`). These criteria are pinned Mathlib theorems and are not restated here.

api.statement: E^b is a G-stable L-subspace containing 0.
A continuous G-equivariant L-linear map E → E′ carries E^b into E′^b, compatibly with identity and composition.
For an isometric action on a normed space, E^b = E.

tests.statement: For the trivial action every vector is G-bounded, since its orbit is a point.
For G = ℤ acting on ℚ_p by n·x = p^nx, a nonzero x is not bounded: |p^nx| = p^{−n}|x| is unbounded as n → −∞.

On a Fréchet space with seminorms (p_i), take a vector v with p_i(v) = 1 for all i and the action of ℤ fixing v. Replacing p_i by i·p_i keeps the topology and v stays bounded, though no single constant bounds all i·p_i(v). The condition is ∀i ∃C_i, not ∃C ∀i.

nodes.title: Étale cohomology as bounded vectors
nodes.statement: Prove that H¹_ét(M^p_{n,C}, L(1)) → H¹_proét(M^p_{n,C}, L(1)) is injective with image exactly the G-bounded vectors (CDN20, Proposition 2.12, line 1020; CDN23, Proposition 5.6, line 2420). The same holds for each M-multiplicity. Prove also that L⊗O(M^p_{n,C}) has no nonzero G-bounded vectors in a supercuspidal sector: O(M^p_{n,C})[M]^b = 0 for supercuspidal M (CDN23, proof of Théorème 5.24(i), lines 2791–2793 and footnote 31). There are two reasons. Bounded functions are constant on connected components. The action of Ǧ on the components factors through Nrd (gap:drinfeld-components), so only one-dimensional JL(M) occur.

tests.statement: Separate seminorm bounds on the pro-étale Fréchet space give a single integral denominator only after the cocompact tree cover. Without it, the argument proves boundedness affinoid by affinoid only.
A constant function on M^p_{n,C} is G-bounded and lies in the trivial sector. Its supercuspidal multiplicity is 0, since dim JL(M) > 1 and Ǧ acts on constants through Nrd.
The rational étale group is L⊗lim_k of integral groups, not lim_k of groups already tensored with L, which would vanish on p^k-torsion.

nodes.title: Bounded duals and universal completions
nodes.statement: Prove the following (CDN23, Lemme 5.3, line 2381; CDN20, Corollaire 2.13, line 1078):

tests.statement: For Π = L trivial, Π′_b = L and every vector is bounded.
For π₀ = St^sm, (b) gives (St^cont)′_b by §4.2.
(c) fails without finite length or admissibility hypotheses on Π; they are part of the statement.

nodes.title: Occurrence and finite length for finite-dimensional Galois representations
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional continuous L-representation V of G_ℚ_p and supercuspidal M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n, prove the following (CDN20, Théorème 2.15, line 1090, with Lemmes 2.17–2.18):

tests.statement: A non-split extension V of V_{M,ℒ} by a character has the quotient V_{M,ℒ}. The theorem applies to it without assuming V semisimple.
For V = V_{M,ℒ}⊕V_{M,ℒ′} with ℒ ≠ ℒ′, Π_M(V) = Π_{M,ℒ}⊕Π_{M,ℒ′} has length two.
For V a character, the Hom into a supercuspidal sector vanishes (§4.6).

nodes.title: Banach multiplicities in differentials
nodes.statement: Let Π be an absolutely irreducible admissible unitary Banach L-representation of G. Prove that Hom_G(Π′_b, L⊗Ω¹(M^p_{n,ℚ_p})) is:

tests.statement: Let π₀ have trivial central character and χ be unramified with χ(p) = 1+p, and put M = M(π₀⊗χ∘det). Then M has level at most n but M ∉ ΦNᵖ, and Hom_G(Π′_{M,ℒ}, L⊗Ω¹(M^p_{n,ℚ_p})) = 0. The printed condition "level ≤ n" would predict ℒ⊗JL(M).
For an ordinary absolutely irreducible Π, Hom_G(Π′_b, (Π^an_{M,ℒ})′_b) = 0 and Hom_G(Π′_b, LL(M)′_b) = 0, so the multiplicity vanishes.
For Π = Π_{M,ℒ}, Hom_G(Π′_b, (Π^an_{M,ℒ′})′_b) = 0 for ℒ′ ≠ ℒ, which bounds the dimension by one.

nodes.title: Banach multiplicities in étale cohomology
nodes.statement: With Π as in §4.12, prove that Hom_G(Π′_b, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,C}, L(1))) is G_ℚ_p×Ǧ-equivariantly and topologically isomorphic to:

tests.statement: The Hom is from Π′_b into cohomology. Reversing the direction would replace V_{M,ℒ} by its dual.
For Π = Π_{M,ℒ} the answer is two-dimensional over L times JL(M), not one-dimensional as in §4.12. The Galois factor V_{M,ℒ} replaces the line ℒ.
For the unramified twist of §4.12 the answer is 0.

nodes.title: Galois multiplicities and vanishing in higher dimension
nodes.statement: For an absolutely irreducible continuous L-representation V of G_ℚ_p, prove that Hom_{W_ℚ_p}(V, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,C}, L(1))) is:

tests.statement: An absolutely irreducible V of dimension three has multiplicity 0.
A character δ with δ(p)² = 1 and δ∘Nrd of level ≤ n contributes through the Steinberg branch. It is not a supercuspidal exception.
The unramified twist with χ(p) = 1+p of §0.1 gives V ≅ V_{M,ℒ} with M ∉ ΦNᵖ. Its multiplicity on M^p_n is 0, although on the full tower it is nonzero.

nodes.title: Arithmetic completed cohomology at fixed level
nodes.statement: Define H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} = lim_k colim_{[K:ℚ_p]<∞} H^{1,+}_{k,K} with its p-adic topology, and H¹_{ℚ̄_p} = L⊗_{O_L}H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p}. The level n stays fixed; only K and k vary (CDN23, §5.3.1, lines 2627–2634). Prove that H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} → H^{1,+}_C := H¹_ét(M^p_{n,C}, O_L(1)) is injective. Its image is the set of almost-smooth classes: those whose reduction modulo p^k is fixed by an open subgroup of G_ℚ_p for every k, the subgroup depending on k (CDN23, Proposition 5.16, line 2635). The route uses the Hochschild–Serre sequence for G_K acting on H^{1,+}_{k,C}. H⁰ of the geometric fibre is finite because M^p_{n,C} has finitely many connected components (gap:drinfeld-components), so colim_K H^j(G_K, H⁰) = 0 for j = 1, 2.

api.statement: H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} and H¹_{ℚ̄_p} are defined by the stated limits. The prime p is inverted after both limits.
The map to H^{1,+}_C is G×Ǧ×G_ℚ_p-equivariant, continuous and injective, with image the almost-smooth classes.
Restriction and corestriction in n commute with the arithmetic and geometric maps; the definition keeps n fixed.

tests.statement: An almost-smooth class may need a smaller open subgroup for each k. Requiring one open subgroup for the whole integral class gives a strictly smaller set in general.
L⊗lim_k is not lim_k(L⊗−): the latter vanishes on the p^k-torsion groups H^{1,+}_{k,K}.
Replacing the fixed level by a limit over n gives a different object. No limit over n enters the factorisation.

nodes.title: Saturation and finite-K pieces
nodes.statement: Prove that H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} is p-torsion-free, p-adically complete and p-saturated in H^{1,+}_C, and that each H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p}/p^k is a smooth G_ℚ_p-module (CDN23, Corollaire 5.17, line 2658). Prove that for every finite K/ℚ_p and k ≥ 1, (H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p}/p^k)^{G_K} with its induced topology is the Pontryagin dual of a smooth O_L[G′]-representation of finite length, where G′ = G/p^ℤ (CDN23, Proposition 5.19, line 2673). The route embeds it continuously into (H^{1,+}_{k,C})^{G_K}, which is profinite and dual to a representation of finite length by gap:modp-drinfeld-finite-length. For compact open H ⊂ G the induced O_L[[H]]-module is finitely generated and separated, so its given topology is the compact module topology.

tests.statement: The invariant piece is compact in its induced topology. Algebraic finite generation over O_L[[H]] alone is not the topological assertion.

p-saturation means that x ∈ H^{1,+}_C with px ∈ H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} lies in H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p}. The sublattice p·H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} is also p-torsion-free and p-adically complete but is not saturated when nonzero: an x outside it has px inside it.
For k = 1 the pieces are duals of smooth k_L[G′]-modules of finite length.

nodes.title: Cohomological block multiplicities
nodes.statement: Use the base roadmap's projective envelope P_B of a block B, E_B = End(P_B) with ordinary composition, and R_B^{ps} (§§5.1–5.4). Define the following (CDN23 lines 2716–2745 and 2757–2769):

api.statement: Evaluation sends f⊗x to f(x), with f·e ⊗ x and f ⊗ e·x identified for e ∈ E_B.
m̌_{n,B} is a compact p-torsion-free O_L-module. It is the O_L-dual of m_{n,B}, not m_{n,B} itself.
m_B(H¹_{ℚ̄_p}) = L⊗m_{n,B}, by compactness of P_B.
G_ℚ_p acts on m_{n,B} by postcomposition and commutes with E_B and with R_B^{ps}.
m_{B,M} = Hom_G(P_B, H¹_{ℚ̄_p}[M]).

tests.statement: If X lies in a block B′ ≠ B, Hom(P_B, X) = 0.
For X = Y⊗JL(M) with Ǧ acting only on the second factor, m_{B,M}(X) ≅ Hom_G(P_B, Y).
The O_L-valued dual m̌_{n,B} is compact, while the Pontryagin dual into L/O_L is discrete. Confusing the two changes the finiteness statement of §5.5.

nodes.title: Integral block evaluation
nodes.statement: Prove that evaluation identifies H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p} with the p-adic completion of ⊕_B m_{n,B}⊗_{E_B}P_B, and that m_{n,B}/p^k ≅ Hom_G(P_B, H^{1,+}_{ℚ̄_p}/p^k) (CDN23, Proposition 5.21, line 2716). The route has four steps:

tests.statement: Modulo p^k each vector has finite block support, but the finite set of blocks may grow with k.
The completed sum is neither the algebraic direct sum nor the product over all blocks. An element with nonzero components in infinitely many blocks, tending to zero p-adically, lies in it.
m_{n,B} is p-torsion-free, so m_{n,B}/p^k → Hom(P_B, X/p^k) is injective. Surjectivity is the content of the lifting step.

nodes.title: Finite generation of the dual multiplicity
nodes.statement: Prove that m̌_{n,B} is a finitely generated R_B^{ps}-module (CDN23, Théorème 5.22, line 2746). This concerns the O_L-dual; m_{n,B} itself is not asserted to be finitely generated. The route uses topological Nakayama. It injects (m_{n,B}/ϖ)[𝔪] into Hom_G(k_L⊗_{R_B^{ps}}P_B, H¹_ét(M^p_{n,C}, k_L(1))). By Paškūnas–Tung (base roadmap §6.7), k_L⊗P_B = π^∨ for a smooth admissible π of finite length. The Hom is then finite-dimensional by gap:modp-drinfeld-finite-length.

tests.statement: The residual Hom is finite-dimensional. Finite length of the arithmetic invariants alone does not bound this geometric multiplicity.
For a block with no constituent in the cohomology, m̌_{n,B} = 0, which is finitely generated.
Topological Nakayama applies because m̌_{n,B} is compact. For the discrete Pontryagin dual it would not.

nodes.title: Type decomposition, level stability and central character
nodes.statement: Prove the following (CDN23, Remarque 5.23, lines 2762–2776):

tests.statement: Level independence holds only after inverting p. Averaging restriction–corestriction over Ǧ_n/Ǧ_{n′} divides by its order, a power of p.
For X = Y⊗JL(M) with the diagonal centre acting trivially, z ∈ Z(G) acts on Y by ω_{JL(M)}(z)⁻¹. Omitting the inverse would give the wrong fixed-determinant ring R_B^{ps,δ_M}.
For special M = Sp⊗δ, δ_M = δ⁻² as a character of ℚ_p^×.

nodes.title: The interpolated Banach dual
nodes.statement: Let M be supercuspidal. Choose a G_ℚ_p-stable R⁺_{B,M}-lattice ρ^{⋄,+} in the R_{B,M}-dual of ρ_{B,M}. Write its Pontryagin dual as colim_i V_i over finite quotients of R⁺_{B,M}, and define Π*(ρ_{B,M}) = L⊗_{O_L} lim_i Π(V_i)^∨, using the integral correspondence of the base roadmap §§3.3 and 3.8 on each finite-length V_i (CDN23, Définition 5.14, line 2606). Prove the following:

api.statement: Π*(ρ) = L⊗lim_iΠ(V_i)^∨ from the stable dual lattice and its finite quotients.
For closed x, κ(x)⊗Π*(ρ) ≅ Π(ρ_x)′_b, G-equivariantly.
Commensurable stable lattices give the same rational object.
Π*(ρ) ≅ Hom^cont_{R_{B,M}}(LL_B(M), R_{B,M}), with the B-adic topology.
If R_{B,M} = 0, then Π*(ρ) = 0.

tests.statement: At a closed point x the fibre is Π(V_{M,ℒ_x})′_b, with ℒ_x the line of the Galois fibre ρ_x (§0.3).
An empty type locus gives zero, not a residual constant family.

Two R_{B,M}-modules can have the same closed fibres and differ by non-separated or non-finite pieces, so the construction must keep the integral limit. Using a lattice in ρ rather than in its dual, with the same integral correspondence, reverses the duality convention.

nodes.title: The special-type convention
nodes.statement: For special M = Sp⊗η, put R_{B,M} = L. If B is the block of St⊗η̄_G, put ρ_{B,M} = η, a character of G_ℚ_p through reciprocity, and Π*(ρ_{B,M}) = (St^cont⊗η_G)′_b. For every other block put ρ_{B,M} = 0 and Π*(ρ_{B,M}) = 0 (CDN23, §5.2, lines 2553–2557).

api.statement: R_{B,M} = L for special M.
In the Steinberg block the Galois factor is η, of rank one, and the G-factor is (St^cont⊗η_G)′_b.
In all other blocks the contribution is zero.

tests.statement: For η = 1 the Galois factor is L with trivial action, not a rank-two semistable extension.
A block not containing St⊗η̄_G contributes zero.
Replacing η by ηχ twists the Galois factor by χ, the G-factor by χ_G and JL(M) by χ_Ǧ. This matches §4.14.

nodes.title: Rigidity over principal ideal domains
nodes.statement: Let A be a principal ideal domain with infinitely many prime ideals, or a finite product of such. Let V and W be representations of G_ℚ_p on finitely generated locally free A-modules whose specialisations at every closed point are absolutely irreducible. If these specialisations are pairwise isomorphic at every closed point, then V ≅ W (CDN23, Lemme 5.12, line 2574). Prove this as follows. Traces agree modulo every maximal ideal, hence agree, since the maximal ideals meet in 0. Irreducibility at the generic point holds, as otherwise almost all specialisations would be reducible. So V and W are isomorphic over the fraction field. Write the intertwiner in Smith normal form P·diag(λ₁,…,λ_d)·Q with λ₁ | ⋯ | λ_d, scaled so that λ₁ is a unit. A non-unit λ_i would make V or W reducible modulo a maximal ideal dividing it. The same statement and proof hold for an A-algebra E that is finite as an A-module, acting A-linearly on V and W and commuting with G_ℚ_p, when the specialisations are absolutely irreducible as modules over (κ(x)⊗_A E)[G_ℚ_p]. The traces of the elements e·g then agree. As in the main case, V and W become absolutely irreducible over (F⊗_A E)[G_ℚ_p], for F the fraction field, and two absolutely irreducible modules with the same trace function are isomorphic by the density theorem.

tests.statement: Over a discrete valuation ring O there is only one closed point. V = ρ and W = ρ⊗χ, with χ a nontrivial unramified character congruent to 1, have isomorphic absolutely irreducible reductions but are not isomorphic. So the hypothesis of infinitely many primes is needed.
For A = L[T] and V = W the statement is trivial.

For A = L[T], a representation that is reducible over L(T) stays reducible modulo all but finitely many maximal ideals. So irreducibility at all closed points forces generic irreducibility; with finitely many closed points this step fails.

For A = L[T] and E = A acting by scalars, E is finite over A but infinite-dimensional over L, and the statement reduces to the one for G_ℚ_p alone. The algebra E_{B,M} of §6.5 is of this kind: it is finite over R_{B,M}, and not finite-dimensional over L unless R_{B,M} is. A version requiring E finite-dimensional over L would not apply there.

nodes.title: The type annihilator
nodes.statement: For p > 2 and supercuspidal M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n, prove that R_B^{ps,δ_M}[1/p] acts on m_{B,M} through its quotient R_{B,M}. Equivalently, I_{B,M} = ker(R_B^{ps,δ_M}[1/p] → R_{B,M}) kills the whole module, not only its closed fibres (CDN23, Théorème 5.24(i), lines 2779–2800). The route has four steps:

tests.statement: Killing every closed fibre does not imply killing the module. Over L[T], the ideal (T) kills N⊗κ(x) for N = L[T]/(T²) at every closed point x, but T·1 ≠ 0 in N.
For special M the statement is immediate from §6.2.
If R_{B,M} = 0, then I_{B,M} is the unit ideal and m_{B,M} = 0.

nodes.title: Structure of the typed multiplicity
nodes.statement: For p > 3, prove that there is an E_B^{δ_M}[G_ℚ_p]-equivariant isomorphism m_{B,M} ≅ m_B^{δ_M}(Π*(ρ_{B,M}))⊗_{R_{B,M}}ρ_{B,M}⊗_{R_{B,M}}Ř_{B,M}. Here Ř_{B,M} = Hom^cont_L(R_{B,M}, L), with (rℓ)(s) = ℓ(rs) (CDN23, Théorème 5.24(ii), lines 2779–2782 and footnote 32, line 2861). The route has five steps:

tests.statement: For R_{B,M} = L (one closed point), Ř = L and the formula reads m_{B,M} ≅ m_B(Π(ρ_x)′_b)⊗ρ_x.
Ř_{B,M} is the continuous L-dual of R_{B,M}. The source formula Ř = Hom(Ř, L) refers to the object being defined (source correction E11).
A comparison of Galois modules alone, without the E_B-action, is weaker than the statement and does not determine the isomorphism.

nodes.title: The factorisation of arithmetic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let p > 3, fix n, and let L contain the fields of definition of all JL(M) of level at most n. Prove that there is a topological L[G_ℚ_p×G×Ǧ]-isomorphism

tests.statement: At a closed supercuspidal point x the multiplicity recovers Π(ρ_x)′_b⊗ρ_x⊗JL(M), in agreement with §4.14.
For the Steinberg block and M = Sp the summand is (St^cont)′_b⊗1⊗1, in agreement with §4.2.
Modulo p^k each integral vector has finite block support, so the unrestricted product over B is not the left side.

nodes.title: The integral-weight automorphy twist
nodes.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, let E_π[k] be E_π as a topological O(Ω)-module with the action g⋆_kℓ = (a−c∂)^{−k}(gℓ) for g = (a b; c d). Negative powers use the automorphism of §2.2 (DLB17, Remarque 11.12, line 2718). Prove that this is an action. Its API:

api.statement: g⋆_kℓ = (a−c∂)^{−k}gℓ, and k = 0 recovers the action on E_π.

The cocycle identity holds for every k ∈ ℤ: for g′ = (a′ b′; c′ d′), (a−c∂)(a′−c′·g∂g⁻¹) = (aa′+bc′)−(ca′+dc′)∂, whose coefficients are the left column of gg′. Since g∂g⁻¹ = (d∂−b)(a−c∂)⁻¹ (§2.2), this is the identity a′(a−cz)−c′(dz−b) = (aa′+bc′)−(ca′+dc′)z.
Under §3.1 the strong dual of E_π[k] realises O(k)(Σ_r)^ρ (DLB17, Remarque 11.12, line 2718; COLMEZ19POIDS lines 310–321 give the same twist in a right-action convention).

tests.statement: At k = 0 every factor is the identity.
aI₂ acts by a^{−k} relative to its action on E_π. Determinant twists must therefore be added separately to keep a central character.
For k = 2, tensoring with det gives the factor det(g)(a−c∂)^{−2}, which is the action on Π(π,2)′_b in the base §6.9.

nodes.title: Weighted realisation and the BGG row
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0, prove the strict exact sequence of G-Fréchet spaces 0 → O(−k)(Σ_r)^ρ → O(k+2)(Σ_r)^ρ⊗det^{k+1} → H¹_dR(Σ_r)^ρ⊗Sym^k → 0, whose first map is (u⁺)^{k+1} = (d/dz)^{k+1} (DLB17, Remarque 11.12, lines 2718–2725). For the identification H¹_dR(Σ_r)^ρ ≅ π′⊗M*_dR of the base §6.9(iii), prove that the preimage of ℒ^⊥⊗(π′⊗Sym^k) in O(k+2)(Σ_r)^ρ⊗det^{k+1} is, up to the twist by the power of det that matches central characters, the strong dual of Π(V^{(k+1)}_{M,ℒ})^an, with V^{(k+1)}_{M,ℒ} the representation of weights {0,k+1} of §2.4. This is COLMEZ19POIDS Conjecture 0.10 (lines 328–332), which its Remarque 0.11(i) and (iii) (lines 333–340) derive from the case k = 0 and its Théorèmes 0.6 and 0.8. For every supercuspidal M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n the same holds on M^p_n, with the identification of §3.3(ii) and the lines ℒ⊗(π′⊗Sym^k). The route takes the case k = 0 from §3.3. Under the twisted actions of §7.1 it identifies the multiplicity space of O(k) with the strong dual of Π(M,k−1) of §2.4, up to a twist, because the operator ∂ of §2.2 corresponds to the operator ∂ of §2.4 (COLMEZ19POIDS Remarque 0.11(ii), lines 335–336). The exact sequences of §2.4(ii) for Π(M,k+1) then give the preimage statement, the first map of the row being u⁺ (Remarque 0.11(i)). Exactness of the row is justified as indicated in DLB17 Remarque 11.12.

tests.statement: For k = 0 the row is the de Rham sequence of §3.3, with O(2)⊗det = Ω¹ (DLB17, Lemme 3.5).
For k = 1, (u⁺)² sends O(−1) to O(3)⊗det². Its cokernel is H¹_dR(Σ_r)^ρ⊗Sym¹ ≅ π′⊗M*_dR⊗Sym¹, which is four copies of π′, and the weights become {0,2}.
The determinant power is k+1; omitting it changes the central character of the middle term by a^{2k+2}.

nodes.title: Comparison with the original first-cover formulation
nodes.statement: Assume that ρ is trivial on 1+ϖ_DO_D. Let Σ_{1+ϖ_DO_D} be the ℚ_p-model of the p^ℤ-quotient of the first ϖ_D-cover, of CDN level 1, and let K = ℚ_{p²}((−p)^{1/(p²−1)}). Since Σ_1 is Galois over Σ_{1+ϖ_DO_D} with group (1+ϖ_DO_D)/(1+pO_D), on which ρ is trivial, the ρ-parts of functions, differentials and de Rham cohomology of Σ_{1+ϖ_DO_D} are those of Σ_1, and §3.3 and the base §6.9 apply to them.

tests.statement: The DLB cover Σ_1 has level 1+pO_D = 1+ϖ_D²O_D. It is not the first ϖ_D-cover (§0.1).
In the basis (ℒ, ℒ′), the diagonal projectivity diag(1, c) fixes the points 0 and ∞ but moves the point 1 unless c = 1.
The comparison is of filtered objects; an unfiltered isomorphism H¹_dR ≅ π′⊗M*_dR does not determine BS(ℒ).

Over ℤ_{p²} the equation y^{p²−1} = p(z−z^p)^{p−1} has special fibre y^{p²−1} = 0, which is not reduced, so no unramified base gives a semistable model of this shape. Over K, with ϖ_K^{p²−1} = −p and y = ϖ_Ky′, it becomes y′^{p²−1} + (z−z^p)^{p−1} = 0, the product of the p−1 factors y′^{p+1} − ζ(z−z^p) over the roots ζ of ζ^{p−1} = −1, which lie in ℚ_{p²}. Each factor reduces to a smooth curve on the vertex affinoid, since ∂/∂z(z−z^p) ≡ 1 mod p, and the p−1 factors match the p−1 connected components of TEI90 Corollary 6.

If ρ is nontrivial on the normal subgroup 1+ϖ_DO_D, which acts trivially on the first cover, every Ǧ-map from ρ to its functions or differentials vanishes. The statement is then empty, so the hypothesis on ρ cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Iwasawa invariants of Drinfeld functions
nodes.statement: For V in the family of π, prove that (O(Σ_r)^ρ)^{diag(p,1)=1} is a free D(Γ)-module of rank two, isomorphic to {μ ∈ H¹(G_ℚ_p, D(Γ)⊗_L V) : ∫_{1+p^mℤ_p}μ ∈ H¹_e(G_{ℚ_p(μ_{p^m})}, V) for every m ≥ 0} (DLB17, Théorème 1.9, line 434; §12.1, line 2785). H¹_e is the image of the Bloch–Kato exponential, not H¹_f or H¹_g. The route identifies the diag(p,1)-fixed vectors with tN_rig(π)^{ψ=1} by §2.1. Applying 1−φ and `allLevelExp_iff_tNrig` with `allLevelExp_oneSubPhi_injective` (PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology §5.7) identifies the result with the right side. Freeness of rank two over D(Γ) is proved here, using the analytic Iwasawa comparison of PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology §5.4 for the right-hand side. The cover level r and the cyclotomic level m are different indices; the source uses n for both (source correction E18).

tests.statement: For V = 0 both sides vanish.
For the trivial representation, H¹_e ≠ H¹_f, which is why the condition uses the exponential image.
The hypothesis of `tNrig_annularGeneration` holds because V is nontrianguline over every finite extension of L. A supercuspidal WD(M) stays irreducible after coefficient extension.

nodes.title: Infinitely primitivable functions
nodes.statement: A function f ∈ O(Σ_n) is infinitely primitivable when it lies in ∩_{j≥0} (d/dz)^j O(Σ_n). Prove that the infinitely primitivable functions lie in H⁰_dR(Σ_n)·O(Ω): finite sums of locally constant functions on geometric components times pullbacks of functions on Ω, after the finite extension that splits the components. The conclusion of DLB17 Théorème 1.10 (line 447), that they lie in O(Ω), is false when component constants are nontrivial (source correction E2). The route decomposes f by Ǧ-types:

tests.statement: On Σ₀ = Ω⊔Ω, f = (1, −1) has the primitives (z^j/j!, −z^j/j!) for every j, but is not a pullback from Ω. So the printed conclusion fails, and the corrected one holds.
For a nontrivial supercuspidal ρ, the infinitely primitivable part of O(Σ_n)^ρ is 0.
The statement is a containment. Not every function of H⁰_dR·O(Ω) is infinitely primitivable, since d/dz is not surjective on O(Ω): H¹_dR(Ω) ≠ 0 (§4.2).

nodes.title: The filtered derived realisation
nodes.statement: For V in the family of π and r large, prove that Hom_{D^b(D(G))}((Π(V)^an)′_b, RΓ_dR(Σ_r)^ρ[1]) ≅ D_dR(V) as filtered L-spaces, canonically up to the common scalar (DLB17, Proposition 12.2, line 2819). Here D^b(D(G)) is the bounded derived category of coadmissible D(G)-modules in the fixed ρ-sector. RΓ_dR(Σ_r)^ρ = [O(Σ_r)^ρ → Ω¹(Σ_r)^ρ] sits in degrees 0 and 1, with F⁰ = [0 → Ω¹(Σ_r)^ρ] and the stupid filtration. The coadmissibility used is that of the ρ-sector; the whole unprojected complex is not asserted to be coadmissible (source correction E8). Construct here the bounded derived category of the fixed-sector coadmissible modules, as an exact subcategory of the coadmissible modules of the base roadmap §0.1. Provide the filtered two-term complex in it and the comparison of its Hom with the filtration. The route uses H⁰_dR(Σ_r)^ρ = 0, so the complex is quasi-isomorphic to H¹_dR(Σ_r)^ρ[−1], and computes Hom to the two-copy smooth quotient by the base §6.9. No Frobenius or monodromy structure is asserted (DLB17, Remarque 12.3(a), line 2823).

tests.statement: For the chosen line ℒ, the filtration induced on the two-dimensional Hom is Fil⁰D_dR(V) = ℒ. An unfiltered dimension count would only give 2.
The trivial sector ρ = 1 has H⁰_dR ≠ 0 and is excluded.

Ǧ acts on O(Σ_r) through the finite group Ǧ/(p^ℤ(1+p^rO_D)), so only finitely many types occur (§0.2). The fixed ρ-sector is used because the comparison with (Π^an/π)′ that gives its coadmissibility (DLB17, Théorème 10.1, line 2192) concerns a supercuspidal ρ, not because the sum over types is infinite. The one-dimensional sectors χ∘Nrd lie outside that comparison (source correction E8).

nodes.title: The boundary-function sheaf
nodes.statement: Let τ: Σ_r → T be the period map to Ω followed by the retraction onto the Bruhat–Tits tree T of PGL₂(ℚ_p). For an open U ⊂ ℙ¹(ℚ_p), let V(U) be the union of rays from a fixed vertex towards points of U, and B_i the ball of radius i. Define F_π as the sheafification of U ↦ colim_i O(τ⁻¹(V(U)∖B_i))^ρ, over the admissible analytic neighbourhoods of DLB17 §12.3 (line 2861). Prove that its restriction maps and G-action do not depend on the vertex or the cofinal sequence of collars. Its identification with tN_rig(π)⊠− is DLB17 Conjecture 12.4 (line 2876) and is not asserted.

api.statement: On a compact open U, sections are the stabilised germs over admissible collars.
Restriction commutes with passage to germs, identities and composition.
Cofinal collar systems and changes of base vertex give canonically isomorphic sheaves.
G transports collars and commutes with restriction and the ρ-projection.

tests.statement: The empty open has zero sections.
Replacing B_i by B_{i+c} for fixed c gives the same germs.

For disjoint compact opens U₁, U₂, deep collars separate, so F_π(U₁ ⊔ U₂) ≅ F_π(U₁)×F_π(U₂). A constant function pulled back from the tree has zero ρ-part for nontrivial supercuspidal ρ, so the projection cannot be omitted.

sourceIssues.statement: Uniqueness of the O(Ω)-module structure needs continuity of f ↦ T_fℓ for every ℓ; algebraic density does not determine an arbitrary action. The base roadmap §6.9 already states uniqueness among continuous module structures.
Infinitely primitivable functions lie in H⁰_dR(Σ_n)·O(Ω), not in O(Ω). §7.5.
A globalisation obtained up to an unramified twist must have the twist removed by a global character before taking isotypic parts. §3.1.
The orthogonal of N⁺_dif,n(V̌) is tN⁺_dif,n(V) for every weight k ≥ 1, not t^kN⁺_dif,n(V). The two agree at k = 1. §1.6.
Injectivity of Res_ℤ_p on the fixed vectors needs the Weyl chart and D_rig^{φ=1} = 0. §2.1.
Generation is used over D(Γ) where only generation after scalar extension to the Robba ring of Γ is available. This roadmap takes tN_rig(π)⊠ℙ¹ from the base roadmap §4.2a and does not use this step.

The displayed computation gives a one-sided inverse of a−c∂; the identity for g⁻¹ gives the other. §2.2. The base roadmap §6.9 already constructs the resolvents, and COLMEZ19POIDS Théorème 0.8(ii) (line 265) proves the two-sided statement for the operator ∂ of §2.4.
Théorème 10.1 gives coadmissibility of the ρ-sector, not of the whole de Rham complex of Σ_n. §7.6.
Infinite t-divisibility must be proved in one lattice of fixed radius on both charts. gap:fixed-radius-divisibility.
Two filtration lines leave a diagonal projectivity; three distinct lines are needed. §7.3.
Ř_{B,M} is the continuous L-dual of R_{B,M}, not Hom(Ř_{B,M}, L). §6.5.
The local statements do not repeat the hypothesis p > 3 used for generic semisimplicity (footnote 32, line 2861; line 93). §§6.5–6.6 retain it.

The completing column uses the symmetric functions without the alternating signs. The proof's complement step checks only AS′ ∩ (S_v+AS_v) = 0, not that S′+AS′ meets S_v+AS_v in 0 (lines 1188–1193). §4.3.
The Hom has dimension 1 when D_pst(V*) ≅ M[−1]* and 0 otherwise, not the reverse. §4.6.
On the p-central quotient the condition is M ∈ ΦNᵖ_n, not level ≤ n; the proofs decompose over ΦNᵖ (line 2434). §§4.12–4.14.
